div.head: Blas 2
div.ab: 7 hæbbe se ðe tyhð cyre swa wæterordal swa isenordal, swa hwæðer swa him leofre sy.
⁊ hæbbe se teond cyre swa wæterordal swa ysenordal, swa hwæþer him leofra sy.
Et sit in arbitrio compellantis ordalium aque uel igniti ferri, quod ei carius (et complacitius) erit.
and hæbbe se teond cyre, swa wæterordal swa ysenordal, swa hwæðer [swa] him leofra sy.
Jedoch habe der Kläger die Wahl: ob Wasserordal oder Eisenordal, welches von beiden ihm lieber ist [von jenem erbracht zu verlangen].
However, let the accuser have the choice: whether water ordeal or iron ordeal, whichever of the two he prefers [to demand that the other undergo].
And the man who is accused shall go to the ordeal, and the accuser shall choose either the ordeal by water or the ordeal by iron—whichever he prefers.]
And the person charged is to go himself to the ordeal, and the accuser to have a choice between water-ordeal and iron-ordeal.
div.note: H omits ‘swa’ after ‘hwæþer’ (also in I Atr 1.3 and III Atr 6). B's ‘cyre’ was later altered to ‘kyre’. Liebermann compares III Atr 6.
